papers.title: From Fill to Freeze: Redesigning homeRNA to Enable Robust Sampling and Scalable Downstream Processing Workflows for Remote Blood Transcriptomics
papers.abstract: In-person research can introduce barriers to participation, including proximity to a study site and scheduling constraints. Our lab developed the homeRNA platform to address these barriers, enabling remote blood collection and RNA stabilization for transcriptomic research. To increase the applicability of homeRNA for large-scale studies, a redesigned version was developed with modifications to 1) improve usability for both participants and downstream processing laboratories, 2) allow for high-throughput manufacturing, and 3) extend the shelf life of the stabilizer tube. In this work, we systematically tested this design against anticipated stresses that can occur throughout a remote study (e.g., high temperature exposure during shipment) to identify and characterize its limitations. We found that the homeRNA device can be prepared and stored at room temperature at least three months in advance of sampling with continued shelf life analysis underway. We also found that the homeRNA platform produces RNA of sufficient quality for downstream transcriptomic analysis under standard shipping durations (i.e., 2 days in transit) and ambient-to-high temperature conditions (i.e., 25-40 {degrees}C) and that RNA quality is unaffected by variable blood volumes collected by participants (mean RIN=7.8 in blood volumes 0.25-1 mL). Lastly, we also found that samples can be stored in typical cold storage temperatures and even up to standard room temperature for at least 4 weeks (mean RIN=8.1 after 4 weeks of storage at -80 to 20 {degrees}C). This work validates that the new homeRNA platform is robust to many of the expected stresses that samples can experience during remote studies.

papers.title: Commensal Engineered Living Materials for Sustained Secretome Delivery and Wound Healing
papers.abstract: Using living cells as dynamic biological factories offers immense potential for the continuous, localized production of therapeutic proteins within compromised tissues. This strategy is particularly compelling for treating chronic non-healing wounds, which lack therapeutics that are able to function effectively in the inflammatory microenvironment. Commensal bacteria have been shown to promote healing in these hostile microenvironments, yet applying live microbes directly onto compromised tissue is clinically unfeasible due off-target safety risks and engraftment challenges. Herein, we establish a well-defined commensal Engineered Living Material (cELM) that allows encapsulation, retention, function, and delivery of native beneficial bacteria for localized production and release of a pro-healing secretome over weeks. We specifically encapsulated a pro-healing human wound bacterial isolate, Alcaligenes faecalis, using biocompatible, click-reactive hydrogel building blocks (thiol- or vinyl-sulfone-functionalized multi-arm poly(ethylene glycol)) and systematically varied the density of the polymer network and of the encapsulated bacteria to establish design rules for creating pro-healing cELMs. Physical confinement in the hydrogel network ensured bacterial biocontainment, while the hydrogel mesh size still permitted diffusion of the therapeutic secretome. Notably, controlling encapsulation density revealed an inverse relationship wherein lower cell densities yielded significantly enhanced per-cell metabolic activity and provided sustained production of pro-healing secreted factors. In a murine diabetic wound model, these A. faecalis cELMs shielded the encapsulated bacteria from host clearance, maintained biocontainment, accelerated re-epithelialization, and improved wound bed maturity. Together, these findings establish design principles for cELMs that couple bacterial biocontainment with sustained secretome delivery, providing a promising platform for localized treatment of chronic wounds.

papers.title: Preserving Nanotherapy-Induced Allogeneic Murine Islet Graft Tolerance During Distal Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Skin Infection
papers.abstract: Eliminating lifelong immunosuppression can make islet transplantation a durable alternative to insulin therapy for type 1 diabetes. As short-course tolerogenic regimens are developed to replace lifelong immunosuppression, it is critical to test their robustness against perturbations such as hospital-acquired infections, which transplant recipients routinely encounter. Herein, we investigated whether rapamycin-loaded polymersomes (rPS), a subcutaneous nanotherapy that induces long-term murine islet allograft survival, can preserve host defenses in a Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) skin infection, and whether the resulting immune response from this distal infection relative to graft location erodes rPS-induced tolerance. rPS maintained neutrophil antibacterial activity despite inhibiting oxidative mechanisms in vitro, and rPS-treated mice demonstrated normal recovery following MRSA challenge. However, MRSA skin infection caused a decline of ~43% in recipient survival for rPS-treated mice, despite surviving recipients retaining glucose-stimulated insulin responsiveness. This erosion of allograft acceptance coincided with a burst of IL-6 within 24h of the infection followed by elevated TNF-[a] and neutrophilia at 13 days post-infection. Combining rPS with a single dose of methylprednisolone reduced IL-6 and TNF- without altering neutrophilia, nearly doubling survival among infected recipients to 80%. Our findings demonstrate that partial dampening of inflammatory insults can restore superior islet allograft acceptance following perioperative infection.

papers.title: Extensional Flow Microfluidics Reveal Size-Dependent Core-Shell Mechanical Heterogeneity in Pancreatic Tumor Spheroids
papers.abstract: Understanding the mechanical behavior of cancer cell aggregates is important for investigating metastatic potential and developing effective therapeutics. Tumor cell clusters are major contributors to metastasis and can undergo extreme deformation to migrate through capillaries smaller than the cluster size, suggesting complex multicellular mechanics. Despite their clinical significance, the mechanics of multicellular spheroids remain underexplored. In this study, the mechanical behavior of spheroids formed from the pancreatic cancer cell line PANC-1 was investigated using a cross-slot microfluidic device. Suspended spheroids from two size ranges were stretched in non-contact extensional flow (small spheroids mostly 40 < D0 < 75 m, large spheroids mostly 90 < D0 < 145 m). Digital image correlation analyses of intra-spheroid strains revealed strong deformation differences for small and large spheroids while analyses based on 2D projected contours of the spheroid shape did not show trends. Smaller spheroids deformed relatively homogeneously and exhibited significant overall stretching. In contrast, larger spheroids displayed heterogeneous deformation characterized by a stiff central core and a deformable outer shell. To investigate the origin of these mechanical differences, cellular morphology and the expression of stiffness-associated proteins, including vimentin and E-cadherin, were assessed from confocal microscopy. Larger spheroids display significantly lower nuclear sphericity than small spheroids, indicating more cellular packing with increasing spheroid size. Additionally, vimentin expression was concentrated in the outer shell of large spheroids, whereas small spheroids exhibit vimentin expression throughout the aggregate. Thus individual cell morphology and cytoskeletal networks seemed to contribute to the core-shell biomechanical behavior of the large spheroids and lack thereof for small spheroids. Taken together, this study suggests that as spheroids grow, they transition from an irregular and disorganized cluster at low cell numbers to a coordinated and hierarchical structure at sufficient cell numbers that corresponds to diameters {gtrsim} 100 m.

papers.title: MitoDecode: quantitative phenotypic decoding of mitochondrial stress states from fluorescence images
papers.abstract: The quantitative measurement of mitochondrial stress from fluorescence images of cells remains a challenging task. Existing methods rely on mitochondrial segmentation, manually predefined features, and discrete phenotype severity classes, which are prone to error and bias. Here, we present MitoDecode, a deep learning network that automatically assesses type and severity of mitochondrial stress from fluorescence microscopy images. MitoDecode eliminates the need for mitochondrial segmentation, is parameter-free, and operates across both diffraction-limited and super-resolution optical imaging modalities. It assigns a phenotypic probability profile for each individual cell, indicating both type and severity of phenotypic stress. The readout thus enables comparisons between different stressors and provides clues for underlying mechanisms. Furthermore, the method captures phenotypic shifts continuously across treatment doses, revealing subtle variations that would otherwise be missed. We demonstrate MitoDecode's adaptability across diverse cell types, imaging modalities, and stress conditions, and show that it can reliably detect mitochondrial phenotypes, even when stressors target non-mitochondrial pathways. We validate the reliability of the model with biochemical assays, showcase its utility for phenotypic stress profiling of drug treatments, and envisage its application for early-stage disease detection, drug discovery, and mechanistic lead generation.

papers.title: Material context and TGF-β blockade timing determine retained matrix in patient-derived bioprinted keratoconus stroma
papers.abstract: Stromal repair requires newly formed matrix to persist while the contractile response to TGF-{beta} is controlled. We developed patient-derived bioprinted gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) stroma to connect material-dependent cell responses with matrix retention after timed receptor blockade. In constructs from six keratoconus (KC) and six normal donors, KC cells retained disease-associated transcription while secreting procollagen I and lumican at normal-donor levels per unit DNA. Comparisons with two-dimensional culture and matched cast GelMA showed that the three-dimensional environment increased matrix induction and lowered resting contractile expression. Printing added a stromal identity response that persisted as retained lumican. Delayed blockade after a TGF-{beta}1 pulse preserved matrix transcription and late secretion. Eleven days after withdrawal, this finite course left more native collagen and lower contractile-gene expression than vehicle in 9/12 donors. Across the tested blockade regimens, at least one regimen achieved both outcomes at the final endpoint in 11/12 donors, including every KC donor. Culture format changed the preferred regimen. Choosing finite blockade by retained collagen instead of secretion changed the schedule in half the donors; the selected arms contained 22.2% more collagen. Retained collagen and contractile expression therefore provide joint endpoints for designing when TGF-{beta}-pathway courses, including losartan and TGF-{beta}3 treatment for keratoconic and scarred corneas, should start and stop.

papers.title: Unlocking Targeted Underwater Delivery of Coral Probiotics
papers.abstract: The rapid global decline of coral reefs has intensified the need for innovative conservation strategies, including microbial therapies to enhance coral health and resilience. A major limitation, however, is the lack of effective delivery systems for administering Beneficial Microorganisms for Corals (BMCs). In this study, we present natural, biodegradable systems for the underwater delivery of probiotic bacteria to corals. Three customized alginate-based delivery formats (beads, hydrogels, and filaments) were developed and loaded with the probiotic Pseudoalteromonas peptidolytica. The materials were loaded with the bacterium at an average concentration of 10^(4) CFU/g of dry polymer and engineered to sink underwater while keeping their structural integrity over time. In vitro assays showed controlled release kinetics, with encapsulated probiotics remaining viable and capable of replication. In vivo experiments compared syringe-based inoculation with the application of alginate beads, hydrogels, and filaments to corals. Microbiome analyses performed before and after inoculation confirmed successful probiotic colonization following deployment of the alginate-based delivery systems. Relative abundance of the probiotic genus Pseudoalteromonas increased markedly in treated corals, reaching 11.5 % after 48 h with alginate beads, 12.7 % after 48 h with hydrogels, and 12.6 % after 24 h with filaments. Furthermore, the degradation mechanisms of the three delivery systems were investigated. As the first biomaterial-based underwater delivery systems specifically engineered for coral probiotics, these alginate-based materials provide a promising foundation for advancing microbial therapies in both controlled aquaria and natural reef environments.

papers.title: 1D model simulations suggest biofilms can suppress cathodic H2 bubble formation
papers.abstract: Microbial electrosynthesis (MES) electrochemically generates H2 for the reduction of CO2 into acetate by acetogens. So far, the importance of a biofilm on the cathode of such systems remains under debate. Here, we investigated the role of cathodic biofilms through computational modelling. We developed MES-BIOFILM, a comprehensive one-dimensional model to simulate steady-state H2 and CO2 concentration gradients within cathodic biofilms, while accounting for the limited solubility of H2. The effects of key biofilm properties, including thickness, cell density and H2 consumption rate were analysed. Overall, our simulations indicate that cathodic biofilms play an important role in (1) minimizing H2 loss from the system through H2 consumption within the biofilm; and (2) suppressing H2 bubble formation by maintaining the H2 concentrations at the cathode surface below saturation. Our model predicts that the current density at which H2 bubbles begin to form can be increased by 5.5-fold relative to a bare electrode when biofilms exhibit a high cell density and high H2 consumption rate. This effect requires biofilms of at least 50 m thickness, whereas CO2 diffusion limitations arise above 200 m. These findings highlight the critical role of biofilms to increase MES performance, while requiring further experimental validation.

papers.title: RNA-triggered Cas12a2 antibacterial activity and resistance plasmid degradation
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) necessitates programmable antibacterial strategies with novel mechanisms. Here, we evaluated an inducible intracellular CRISPR/Cas12a2 system in engineered Escherichia coli targeting a chloramphenicol-resistance (Chl) transcript. Cas12a2 activation significantly delayed bacterial growth and reduced recoverable colony-forming units (CFU) by 3-log10 in vitro, and reduced bacterial burdens in a mouse skin wound model. Transcriptomic profiling revealed upregulation of recA, a key mediator of the SOS response. We therefore designed a Chl-recA dual-targeting construct, which produced a greater growth delay than either single-targeting counterpart. The optimized dual-targeting system led to an approximately 4-log10 reduction in bacterial burden in vivo. Furthermore, exploratory qPCR of culture supernatants suggested a treatment-associated decrease in amplifiable plasmid DNA. Overall, this study provides proof-of-concept for resistance-transcript-guided Cas12a2 antibacterial activity and highlights the potential of co-targeting stress-associated transcripts to enhance programmable antimicrobials.

papers.title: Rapid Electro-optic Two-photon Bessel Light Sheet Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging for Tissue Volume Interrogation
papers.abstract: We report a two-photon light sheet electro-optic fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (TPLS-EO-FLIM) technique based on an electro-optic (EO) modulation detection module. Scanning two-photon Bessel light sheet excitation was used to achieve in-depth volumetric imaging. The low cross-section of multiphoton excitation requires high detection efficiency, and electro-optic detection enables fast wide-field FLIM with a scientific complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (sCMOS) detector. Phototoxicity is minimized by utilizing signal from the entire illuminated sample area in a wide field camera exposure, and time-resolved volume acquisitions are feasible in minutes, with cross-sectional field of view and light sheet length over 300 microns. The method has sub-nanosecond lifetime resolution and is capable of accurate FLIM images in 10 ms exposures with as low as a few hundred photons per pixel. The technique was demonstrated through volumetric FLIM of a green fluorescent protein (GFP) labeled zebrafish embryo heart, of multi-fluorescent protein (multi-FP) labeled plant root structures and of dynamic cardiac cycles in live zebrafish embryos. For the latter, we recorded the cardiac cycle dynamics of a zebrafish embryo at 50 frames per second and measured biomechanical parameters such as heart rate, ventricle/atrium areas, atrioventricular valve dynamics, and fractional area change. Taken together, these studies show the capability of the system for rapid, high resolution, and functional imaging in diverse biological contexts.

papers.title: Large-scale AI-guided discovery of antifreeze peptides reveals functional tandem-repeat architectures
papers.abstract: Despite growing demand for biocompatible materials that regulate ice crystallization in cryopreservation, antifreeze peptide discovery remains constrained by limited candidate sequence diversity and reliance on known protein scaffolds. Here, we establish an AI-guided discovery framework integrating multimodal antifreeze protein prediction, generative sequence expansion and local sequence-pattern analysis. AFPFusionLM combines protein sequence and structure-aware representations, achieving an AUROC of 0.937 and an AUPRC of 0.957 on an independent reference set. Antifreeze-domain-adapted protein sequence generation and multimodel consensus screening of UniProt, glacier metagenomes and generated sequences yielded 87,305 candidate protein records. Large-scale sequence analysis revealed recurring periodic sequence architectures across multiple candidate protein clusters, enabling the identification of short-peptide families with shared repeat features and their natural variants. Experimental evaluation revealed ice recrystallization inhibition activity in multiple peptides from repeat-associated families, with inhibitory effects comparable to or greater than those of reference peptides reported in the literature. Cell-based experiments using a representative peptide-containing formulation also supported its cryoprotective potential under reduced-DMSO conditions. These findings show that large-scale sequence exploration can reveal function-associated peptide sequence architectures, providing a research framework for the systematic discovery and subsequent optimization of antifreeze peptides.

papers.title: Metabolic engineering of Saccharomyces cerevisiae for improved polyphosphate production
papers.abstract: Finite high-grade phosphate rock reserves and rising legislative demand for phosphorus recycling create a need for processes converting phosphorus-containing residual streams into valuable products. Microbial synthesis of inorganic polyphosphate (polyP) could complement its energy-intensive chemical manufacturing while enabling phosphorus recovery in a value-added product with applications ranging from food processing to flame retardants and fertilizer. After orthophosphate (Pi) starvation and refeeding, Saccharomyces cerevisiae naturally accumulates polyP as a cellular Pi reserve, but the current multistage process complicates industrial implementation. Here, we identified metabolic interventions that uncouple polyP accumulation from Pi starvation by systematic evaluation of 57 engineered S. cerevisiae CEN.PK113-7D strains. Constitutive activation of the PHO regulon produced the strongest increase in polyP, whereas disruption of inositol pyrophosphate synthesis, Pi import, or the vacuolar transporter chaperone complex impaired accumulation. This pattern indicates that efficient polyP accumulation depends on coordinated activation of Pi acquisition and vacuolar polymerization. Notably, deletion of PHO80 converted a transient starvation response into a constitutive production phenotype, enabling high polyP accumulation during growth. Optimization of the growth medium increased the polyP content further, and efficient use of the supplied Pi was demonstrated, while electron microscopy paired with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy supported increased vacuolar storage. During aerobic exponential fed-batch cultivation, pho80{Delta} simultaneously formed biomass and polyP, reaching a polyP content of 22.1% of cell dry weight and a titer of 8.2 g/L, both expressed as KPO3 equivalents. These findings establish S. cerevisiae pho80{Delta} as a promising platform for biological polyP production and phosphorus recovery.

papers.title: Biological Signaling Pathways Associated with Late Tendon Development in Chicken Embryos and Their Dependence on Mechanical Stimulation
papers.abstract: During embryonic and neonatal development, tendons exhibit rapid changes in mechanics and structure, including increases in collagen content, crosslinking, and fibril length. These functional and structural changes are partly dependent on mechanical stimulation. However, the specific mechanobiological mechanisms driving these changes remain poorly understood. The objective of this study was to identify the potential biological mechanisms and pathways driving tendon maturation into load-bearing materials using an embryonic chick model. Using bulk RNA sequencing, gene set enrichment analysis, and transcription factor analysis, we produced a transcriptomic profile of chick hindlimb tendons during late embryonic development (E16, E18, and E20) and tendons from rigid and flaccid paralysis-treated embryos. Additionally, we assessed the results from two differential expression analysis models to improve the replicability of our findings. Our results suggest that the largest transcriptomic response occurs between embryonic day 16 and 20, and that among paralysis conditions, rigid paralysis produces the greatest effect relative to controls. Across development, we found positive enrichment in processes related to mechanotransduction, extracellular matrix remodeling, cell adhesion, and contractility, and identified candidate pathways upregulated with development, including TGF-{beta}, PI3K-AKT-mTOR, Hippo, circadian rhythm, and focal adhesion signaling. In paralysis-treated embryos, our data suggest impairment in extracellular matrix remodeling and mechanotransduction events. Specifically, we found that both modes of paralysis are associated with a cellular stress response and downregulation of WNT signaling. Together, our findings identify candidate mechanotransduction pathways that are associated with late tendon maturation and altered by paralysis, which may inform tendon tissue engineering and regenerative approaches.

papers.title: Cascaded Dual-Targeting (WTW/TAT) Liposomes Delivery DOX for Precision Glioblastoma Treatment
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains difficult to treat because the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and blood-tumor barrier (BTB) severely limit drug transport into tumor tissue. To address these delivery constraints, we developed a dual-targeted liposomal nanoplatform (WT-LIP) that integrates a WTW dual-targeting peptide to promote receptor-mediated BBB transcytosis and specificity to GBM and a TAT peptide to enhance post-barrier penetration and tumor-cell uptake, enabling sequential barrier crossing and GBM targeting. DOX@WT-LIP efficiently encapsulated doxorubicin (DOX) and increased endothelial transport in vitro, achieving a permeated dose of 60.74 {+/-} 2.14% at 480 min, while producing deeper transendothelial penetration and greater downstream tumor killing in a BBB/GBM co-culture. In orthotopic U251-luc models, DiD-labeled WT-LIP showed enhanced brain/tumor accumulation (G/B = 2.16 {+/-} 0.06), and DOX@WT-LIP markedly suppressed tumor growth (74.92% inhibition), improved survival, and exhibited comparatively reduced systemic toxicity. This work highlights a ligand-guided strategy that couples efficient BBB transport with tumor-selective delivery to improve GBM chemotherapy.

papers.title: Live Droplet Single-Cell RNA Sequencing
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing has emerged as one of the most influential methods of the past decade, enabling the dissection of cellular heterogeneity and the discovery of rare cell types. However, most workflows require cell lysis and provide only terminal snapshots, limiting their ability to capture dynamic cellular trajectories and temporal variations within the same cell. Herein, we present Live Droplet single-cell RNA sequencing (Live D-seq), a technology that enables scalable transcriptome-wide profiling of individual living cells over time. Live D-seq combines longitudinal intracellular sampling of live, barcoded cells with particle-templated emulsification and barcoded hydrogel beads, enabling repeated samples from the same cell lineage to be linked across time points. We showcase Live D-seq's capabilities by (i) demonstrating minimal cross-contamination in cross-species experiments, (ii) precisely mapping cellular barcodes to hydrogel bead barcodes, and (iii) tracking epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition dynamics in A549 cells over time. Altogether, Live D-seq enables repeated, non-destructive measurements of gene expression in the same single cells, offering a framework to study longitudinal single-cell biology in health and disease.

papers.title: Transferrin receptor binding valency determines the circulating half-life and weight-loss efficacy of Fc-FGF21 in TfR-humanized mice
papers.abstract: Fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21) is a promising metabolic hormone with potent anti-obesity effects. It acts in both the central nervous system and peripheral tissues to exert its metabolic benefits. Because its receptors are expressed at low levels in the brain, we hypothesized that enhanced transport across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) would improve its efficacy. To achieve this, FGF21 was fused to Fc(TV35), an engineered Fc fragment that binds the human transferrin receptor (hTfR), to generate Fc(TV35)-FGF21. Fc(TV35)-FGF21 does not bind to mouse TfR, so it produced weight-loss effects in wild-type diet-induced obese mice comparable to those of Fc-FGF21. However, it failed to induce weight loss in homozygous hTfR-humanized mice because of a markedly shortened circulating half-life. Converting Fc(TV35)-FGF21 from a homodimer to a bispecific Fc format with a single hTfR-binding arm partially restored the circulating half-life and weight-loss efficacy. Reducing mouse hTfR zygosity from homozygous to heterozygous did not substantially improve the engineered protein's half-life or weight-loss effect. Taken together, our findings suggest that sustained systemic exposure is a major determinant of FGF21's weight-loss efficacy and that hTfR engagement can shorten its systemic half-life and compromise its therapeutic activity. These results highlight an important design limitation of TfR-based brain vehicles, especially for delivering metabolic hormones with low-abundance CNS receptor targets. As a result, further optimization of shuttle formats to minimize systemic clearance while crossing the BBB is needed for metabolic hormones.

papers.title: Bicarbonate-free pH neutralization resensitizes ovarian cancer to chemotherapy and is tracked by 3T CEST MRI
papers.abstract: Ovarian tumors that initially respond to platinum-taxane chemotherapy often relapse as chemoresistant disease. The acidic tumor microenvironment is a well-known but under-exploited driver of this resistance, and neutralization strategies such as oral bicarbonate have not translated. Here we show that inhibiting specific tumor pH regulators at noncytotoxic doses relieves acidosis and restores frontline chemotherapy, monitored noninvasively at clinical 3T. In OVCAR3 and SKOV-3 ovarian cancer cells, MCT1 and MCT4 were overexpressed under acidosis, and the MCT4 inhibitor acriflavine reduced extracellular acidification at concentrations well below its cytotoxic IC50, without bicarbonate buffering. Acidosis blunted the efficacy of both paclitaxel and carboplatin, raising their IC50 values, which acriflavine reversed. In SKOV-3 tumors, acidoCEST MRI with iopromide noninvasively measured baseline tumor acidosis and its normalization following acriflavine treatment. These results establish tumor acidosis as an imageable, druggable determinant of chemoresistance and a bicarbonate-free therapeutic target.

papers.title: Wearable Estimation of Knee Joint Contact Forces: SiMPLeSENSE, a Simulated-IMU Pipeline Validated Against In Vivo Loads
papers.abstract: Knee joint compressive forces (KCF) are central to understanding joint loading and degeneration, but they can be measured directly only with instrumented implants. Musculoskeletal models provide a non-invasive alternative, and inertial measurement units (IMUs) could make such estimates portable. However, no dataset combines IMU signals with in vivo implant forces, so the accuracy of IMU-based KCF remains unverified. We developed SiMPLeSENSE, a framework that derives virtual IMU orientations from optical motion capture using subject-specific SMPL meshes. Using the CAMS-Knee dataset, we reconstructed kinematics with OpenSense and estimated KCF in OpenSim with a Rapid Muscle Redundancy solver, comparing the estimates with in vivo measurements during level walking and stair descent. We also assessed robustness to sensor placement error by adding empirically derived thigh and shank orientation noise (for two cases). Across subjects and activities, the simulated-IMU estimates closely tracked the optical mocap-driven estimates and reproduced the in vivo force pattern, with the agreement against the optical reference being higher for stair descent. Overall, the estimated forces matched the in vivo measurements with a median RMSE of about 0.3 to 0.5 BW and correlations near 0.95. Adding realistic orientation error increased RMSE only modestly, whereas doubling it markedly overestimated peak force, most evident for stair descent. These results indicate that the approach is robust to substantial changes in input kinematics, supporting a laboratory-independent setup combining inertial motion capture, a small EMG set, and instrumented force shoes for home and clinical monitoring of knee loading.

papers.title: An Efficient Microfluidic Platform for Organ-Specific CyclicMultiaxial Loading and Differentiation of Progenitor Cells
papers.abstract: Mechanical loading is a fundamental regulator of tissue development, maturation, and function, yet existing in vitro systems predominantly apply uniaxial load/strain to cell-laden hydrogels, limiting their ability to reproduce physiologically relevant multiaxial on-chip tissue mechanics. Here, we present an engineered system to apply controlled multiaxial mechanical loading to real scaffolds with undifferentiated cells. The system enables programmable cyclic stretching and relaxation at the cell scaffold level and is compatible with both cell-laden native scaffold and engineered soft tissues. We have quantified the strain field experienced by the tissue with distinct mechanical loading periods using computation simulations and validated these with systematic experiments, demonstrating reproducible and various organ-relevant multiaxial strain profiles. As proof of concept, we applied the approach to human cardiac tissues, where cyclic multiaxial mechanical loading of mononuclear cells laden native tissue scaffold promoted cardiac structural organization and supports the emergence of spontaneous contractile activity. This approach provides a generalizable method for reproducing physiologically relevant tissue mechanics in vitro and enables systematic investigation of mechano-regulation across a plethora of human tissues.

papers.title: Material-driven fibronectin assembly enables low-dose BMP-2 to regenerate structurally mature bone in critical-sized load-bearing defects
papers.abstract: Bone grafts for critical-sized load-bearing defects are usually judged by how much bone forms, and rarely by whether that bone is structurally and mechanically competent. Here, degradable ceramic monetites coated with poly(ethyl acrylate) (PEA) and functionalised with fibronectin (FN) and rhBMP-2 at 10-25 g/mL, 60-150-fold below the approved clinical concentration, are assessed across length scales. MicroCT showed that only monetites functionalised with rhBMP-2 bridged the defect, with a significant increase in new bone volume in both the monetite vicinity and the whole defect volume. In contrast, platelet-rich plasma (PRP) functionalisation significantly reduced bone formation relative to FN, showing that the identity of the adhesion cue, and not merely its presence, determines the outcome. Monetite degradation and increased interconnected porosity favoured bone ingrowth and produced a continuous interface between monetite and new bone. The multiscale analyses of quantitative polarised light microscopy, SAXS and nanoindentation show that PEA-coated monetites functionalised with FN and 25 g/mL rhBMP-2 promoted structurally and mechanically more mature bone, with a hierarchical organisation and local mechanical properties approaching those of native cortical tissue. In the bridged region this group recapitulated the preferential collagen fibre orientation of native cortical bone and reached an elastic modulus and hardness that were not statistically distinguishable from it, although mineral particles throughout the regenerated tissue remained thicker and less aligned than in cortical bone. Synchrotron microCT in an ovine model extended these findings to a clinically relevant scale, supporting the translational potential of the system. Taken together, these findings position PEA-coated monetites functionalised with FN and low-dose rhBMP-2 as a strategy for the structural and functional regeneration of large bone defects.

papers.title: Establishing de novo microbial biosynthesis of anisole
papers.abstract: Anisole is a valuable aromatic ether and promising green solvent whose industrial manufacture relies exclusively on petroleum-derived phenol and hazardous alkali-mediated methylation. Here, we establish the first de novo microbial biosynthesis of anisole from glucose in Pseudomonas putida KT2440 by integrating retrosynthetic pathway design with growth-coupled directed evolution. Using a selection platform in an engineered double auxotroph, in which growth depends on S-adenosylmethionine-dependent methylation, we evolved a promiscuous plant chavicol O-methyltransferase to yield phenol O-methyltransferase 1 (POMT1; bearing a key D264N substitution), which improved anisole production by 2.3-fold over the wild-type enzyme. To overcome product volatility, we integrated an in situ two-phase extraction system using dodecane that achieved near-quantitative product recovery. Then, we compared two phenol routes from the shikimate pathway, selected the 4-hydroxybenzoate route, and raised precursor supply by deleting competing reactions and introducing feedback-resistant and reduced-flux variants in two shikimate pathway enzymes. The final strain produced up to 0.57 mM anisole (62 mg/L) from glucose.

papers.title: NPlasmid-seq: Cas9-encoded terminal signatures enable molecule-level nanopore quality control of vector and IVT-template plasmids
papers.abstract: Consensus-based plasmid quality control can overlook structural heterogeneity within a preparation. We developed NPlasmid-seq, a Cas9-guided nanopore workflow that encodes sample identity through paired terminal signatures generated at predefined backbone positions, without sample-specific oligonucleotide barcodes. We cleavage-validated 24 sgRNAs. In five representative assigned read bins, each bin showed its strongest sequence agreement with its cognate reference. Contaminant detection was evaluated with a single class-specific classifier applied both to computational read mixtures and to physical DNA mixtures, placing the two designs on a common scale. In computational read mixtures of 5,000 reads, a contaminant was detected in all 20 independent subsamples at each of 0.2%, 0.5%, 1% and 5% abundance and in 13 of 20 subsamples at 0.1%; precision was 1.000 in all 100 subsamples, with no false-positive calls among 493,200 reads from the declared target plasmid. In physical DNA mixtures carried through cleavage, pooled library preparation and sequencing, a contaminant was detected in all six samples prepared at 0.5 mol% input and all six at 1 mol%. Observed read fractions did not distinguish the 0.5 and 1 mol% input levels. Instead, they differed systematically by 4.0-fold between preparation pools, a larger effect than the difference between the two input levels. We therefore interpret the workflow as a detector, not a quantifier, of sub-percent contamination. Read-level analysis identified a recurrent 93-bp deletion in 61.7% of reads from a preparation that had passed consensus-based quality control. Sanger genotyping of 24 colonies identified deletion-type profiles in 10 colonies and intact-type profiles in three. The remaining 11 colonies showed double peaks at the diagnostic locus, consistent with coexistence of both sequence forms within individual clones. In in vitro transcription template plasmids, longer poly(A) tracts were associated with higher multimeric-read fractions. Across ten matched A90 culture pairs, propagation at 30 degree reduced these fractions relative to 37 degree (paired t-test, P = 0.0098). These measurements describe recovered read populations, not absolute molecular abundances. NPlasmid-seq therefore complements consensus validation by revealing sequence and structural heterogeneity within a preparation and by identifying a culture condition associated with a lower multimeric-read fraction.

papers.title: Differential sensing with imprinted and non-imprinted organic electrochemical transistors reduces calibration drift in wearable sweat cortisol sensors
papers.abstract: The output of a wearable cortisol sensor drifts over days for reasons unrelated to cortisol, so a calibration made on the first day soon stops being valid. In our differential organic electrochemical transistor, a PEDOT:PSS transistor coated with a molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) for cortisol is paired with one coated with a non-imprinted polymer (NIP) of the same composition, and the NIP response is subtracted. Over four calibrations in artificial sweat across 14 days, the response of the MIP alone shifted by 15% to 22% of its range on day 1, whereas the differential output shifted by 1% to 10%, and the variation between days at 1 to 10nM fell by 65% to 70% on average for individual pairs. In sweat from one participant, read against the calibration from day 1, both outputs tracked the direction of visible changes in salivary cortisol, while the MIP alone diverged from the differential output, consistent with the laboratory drift.

papers.title: Stop-Flow Lithography Using Hydrodynamic Flow Resistance Regulation and Hydraulic Compliance Minimization for Size-Tunable Anisotropic Multilayered Microparticles Fabrication
papers.abstract: Stop-flow lithography (SFL) enables the fabrication of microparticles with designed geometries and material compositions, but its performance relies on rapid flow stopping, which remains particularly challenging in multi-inlet systems with high hydrodynamic flow resistance and hydraulic compliance. Here, we develop a pneumatic-controlled SFL platform with a framework based on flow resistance regulation and hydraulic compliance minimization for fabricating size-tunable anisotropic multilayered microparticles. Our analysis indicates that flow-stopping behavior is governed by the release of extra fluid volume stored in the system due to hydraulic compliance, which arises from the deformation of microfluidic components and the compressibility of the fluid within them. Through numerical modeling and analysis, we identify deformation in the PDMS inlet port region as the dominant contributor to the stored extra fluid volume. By regulating the flow resistance of the tubing relative to that of the outlet channel, the stored extra fluid volume can be preferentially released forward through the outlet or backward through the inlet tubing, enabling rapid flow stopping across configurations with 500, 250, and 100 m outlets. Furthermore, by supporting the PDMS membrane beneath the inlet region with a rigid glass substrate and reducing its dimensions, the hydraulic compliance and consequently the stored extra fluid volume are significantly reduced. With these strategies, microparticles with well-defined boundaries can be fabricated at short, flow-stopping, delay times, and the flow profiles obtained in multi-inlet systems can be preserved during flow stopping and transferred into particle patterns.

papers.title: Quantum Dot-Based Non-invasive Monitoring of Sinusoidal Endothelial Scavenger Function in Steatohepatitis
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and its progressive form, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), represent urgent medical challenges. Current non-invasive assessments rely on serum indices or tissue stiffness, and none visualizes functional changes within the liver, hindering drug discovery and patient management. In this study, we developed a non-invasive technique using semiconductor quantum dots, as blood-borne foreign particle mimics, to evaluate the scavenger function of liver sinusoidal endothelial cells (LSECs) via near-infrared optical imaging. Progression from MASLD to MASH induced a significant decline in the scavenger capability of LSECs, resulting in a marked reduction of intrahepatic quantum dot retention. Mechanistically, we demonstrated that quantum dots are recognized and internalized by scavenger receptor class A (SR-A) on LSECs, and that SR-A-mediated uptake progressively diminishes with increasing MASH severity. Crucially, quantum dot retention levels significantly correlated with both the progression and regression of MASH pathology. These findings demonstrate that quantum dot-based optical evaluation of LSEC scavenger function offers a highly sensitive, non-invasive diagnostic platform for staging MASH and assessing therapeutic efficacy.

papers.title: Fibronectin-Assisted Coating of Low-Molecular-Weight Fucoidan Creates a Biomimetic Interface for Endothelialization of Cobalt-Chromium Stents
papers.abstract: Incomplete or delayed endothelialization after stent implantation compromises vascular healing and increases the risk of restenosis and late thrombosis. To address this limitation, Cobalt-Chromium (Co-Cr) stents were modified with a biomimetic coating combining Low-Molecular-Weight Fucoidan (LMWF), a sulfated polysaccharide with glycocalyx-mimetic properties, and fibronectin, to promote endothelial repair while preserving vascular homeostasis. The morphology, chemical composition, wettability and stability of the coating were characterized using complementary physicochemical approaches. The behavior of human endothelial cells cultured on this dual fibronectin-LMWF-coated stent was then assessed. Our results showed that fibronectin-LMWF-based coating achieved a ten-fold higher surface density on the stent than LMWF alone (0.29 {+/-} 0.04 vs 0.03 {+/-} 0.01 {micro}g/mm2) and retained 0.27 {+/-} 0.03 {micro}g/mm2 of the coating after 168 h, compared with 0.01 {+/-} 0.01 {micro}g/mm2 for LMWF alone. Although wettability remained similar to that of uncoated stents, the combined coating markedly enhanced endothelial cell adhesion, spreading, lamellipodia formation, proliferation, and MMP-2 secretion. These effects were accompanied by enhanced F-actin organization and redistribution of membrane-associated VE-cadherin, integrins {beta}1 and 6, and syndecans-1 and -4, without major changes in their total expression. Importantly, the coating induced these responses without detectable cytotoxicity or significant inflammatory activation. Overall, the fibronectin-LMWF-based coating provides a stable biomimetic interface that enhances endothelialization through coordinated remodeling of adhesion, cytoskeletal, and glycocalyx-associated structures, while maintaining endothelial homeostasis on Co-Cr stent. This strategy offers a promising platform for next-generation glycocalyx-like stent coatings designed to improve vascular healing and limit restenosis.

papers.title: A cytotoxicity dataset for data-driven design of ionizable lipid nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are widely used to deliver nucleic acid therapeutics, but the design of safe LNPs remains challenging due to the complex activity relationships among structure, composition, and physicochemical properties. Here, we present a curated dataset, the Lipid Nanoparticle Cytotoxicity Database (LNPCD), which aggregates 1,413 LNP cytotoxicity measurements across 1,288 unique ionizable lipids drawn from 11 high-throughput combinatorial studies. Lipid structures were generated computationally from the published libraries and manually verified against the original publications. Each record pairs a machine-readable SMILES representation of the ionizable lipid with its measured viability endpoint and the associated experimental descriptors, including cell line, dose, and cargo type. The dataset provides a traceable resource for examining how ionizable lipid structure and experimental conditions relate to in vitro cell viability, and for developing and evaluating computational models of lipid nanoparticle cytotoxicity.

papers.title: A compact three-way junction oligonucleotide probe for widefield and super-resolution imaging of RNAs and proteins
papers.abstract: Molecular imaging of RNAs and proteins requires methods that preserve nanoscale organization while enabling large-scale tissue analysis. However, weak or low-abundance targets often need signal amplification, which can increase labeling size, background, or signal spread and compromise super-resolution imaging. Here, we report a compact three-way junction (3WJ) oligonucleotide probe platform for multiscale RNA and protein imaging. The design couples paired target recognition with junction assembly and recruitment of preassembled amplifier complexes, while tunable amplification balances signal strength and labeling size. Using DNA origami and single-molecule localization microscopy, we show enhanced signal while retaining the ability to resolve nanoscale target patterns. The platform improves RNA detection and supports simultaneous RNA-protein super-resolution imaging in cells. It also enhances protein detection in formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissues under low-numerical-aperture, large-field imaging conditions. Together, this programmable 3WJ platform enables sensitive RNA and protein detection across scales, supporting super-resolution analysis of molecular organization and large-field tissue mapping.

papers.title: N-GLYcanyzer monitoring of a microperfusion process reveals critical parameters' impact on Trastuzumab biosimilar N-glycoform time evolution
papers.abstract: Controlling monoclonal antibody (mAb) N-glycosylation as a critical quality attribute (CQA) remains challenging in continuous and intensified biomanufacturing, where conventional end-point analyses obscure dynamic pathway responses. Here, we deployed the N-GLYcanyzer process analytical technology (PAT) for automated monitoring of a microperfusion process that reveals critical parameters' impact on Trastuzumab biosimilar N-glycoform time evolution across a 20-day culture duration of Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cells in a ~2 mL scale-down microbioreactor perfusion platform. Using offline PAT assays combined with our integrated at-line PAT workflow, we systematically screened six perfusion process parameters: carbon source, viable cell density (VCD), perfusion rate, temperature, and pH. While nutrient limitation and thermal/acidic stress significantly disrupted N-glycans maturation, notably triggering high-mannose (Man5) accumulation and severe productivity penalties under pH 6.7 and 39 {degrees}C operation, targeted feed supplementation with galactose and MnCl2 consistently shifted glycoform profiles away from G0F toward galactosylated species (G1F, G1F', G2F). Crucially, coupling this combined feed strategy with an intensified perfusion rate (1.2 VVD) achieved a sustained, desired galactosylation shift without a productivity cost. These findings demonstrate that nutrient feed composition and perfusion rate are primary levers for steering continuous intensified microperfusion processes for biologics production with desired N-glycoform states and highlight the utility of automated at-line PAT like N-GLYcanyzer for enabling real-time attribute-based control in continuous biomanufacturing.

papers.title: An Improved Manufacturing Method for Infusible Extracellular Matrix Materials to Enable Efficient Scale-Up, Improved Efficacy, and Clinical Translation
papers.abstract: Decellularized extracellular matrix (ECM) materials are a popular choice for tissue engineering and regenerative medicine applications due to their multifaceted bioactive capabilities arising from their heterogenous composition. For minimally invasive delivery, infusible ECM (iECM) was developed through fractionation of digested decellularized ECM, allowing the material to be safely delivered intravascularly. iECM localizes to permeable vasculature in inflamed tissues and exerts immunomodulatory and pro-reparative effects with proof-of-concept already demonstrated in multiple preclinical models including myocardial infarction (MI) and multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS). However, one major limitation of iECM is the steps required for manufacturing, involving centrifugation, dialysis/lyophilization, and filtration (C-D-F). These steps limit manufacturing output and iECM concentration, and require significant human handling, limiting compliance with current good manufacturing practices (cGMP). To overcome these challenges, we developed a method for manufacturing iECM that utilizes depth filtration and tangential flow filtration (DF-TFF), which reduces manufacturing time, allows for increased iECM concentration, and reduces human manipulation of material, improving translatability and scalability of iECM materials. Based on multiple material characterization methods, we determined that iECM made with DF-TFF was comparable to iECM made with C-D-F. By increasing iECM concentration through this manufacturing method, we demonstrate a dose dependent response in an acute MI porcine model and a mouse MODS model. Finally, DF-TFF enabled timely production of iECM from alternative tissue sources. Altogether, DF-TFF allows for improvements in production time, scale-up, cGMP compliance, and increased dose through higher concentration, paving the way for future clinical translation as well new preclinical studies.
